subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan - EnterpriseFin
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Chen <tom.chen@enterprisefin.com>, Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@enterprisefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan - EnterpriseFin

Hi Tom / Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time to join today's demo. Great conversation — appreciate you walking through the integration goals. Per our call, below is a concise recap and a proposed 3-week POC plan so your team can validate performance, latency, and cost for the customer-facing case you described.

Recap (what we covered)
- Use case: in-product context-aware guidance and document summarization for advisor workflows
- Targets: sub-200ms 95th-pct latency for <512 token requests; per-user cost goal ~$0.002 per query
- Integrations: Send content via secure API to a private instance (VPC) for PII-sensitive flows

Proposed POC: 3-week plan (high level)
1) Week 0 (Prep, 3 business days)
   - Share success criteria spreadsheet (attached) and data/sample payload examples
   - Provide SOC2 and network requirements; confirm test dataset
   - Proposal owner: Dylan Brooks (AE) / Camila Reyes (Solutions)
2) Week 1 (Integration + baseline)
   - EnterpriseFin integrates sandbox API keys and runs baseline traffic (1000 synthetic queries)
   - Redwood provides a tuned model instance and initial batching/quantization config
   - Success metric: baseline latency & cost per token measured across sample set
3) Week 2 (Workload validation)
   - Run representative traffic from advisor UI; enable prefix/KV caching for repeated context
   - Success metric: stability under ~50 concurrent sessions; >=95% pass for latency SLO
4) Week 3 (Evaluation + handoff)
   - Final eval report (latency, cost, error rates) and recommended production config
   - Decision: go/no-go for expanded pilot or Dedicated capacity

Success criteria (attached spreadsheet):
- Functional correctness: >=90% on a set of 50 curated prompts (manual review)
- Latency: 95th pct <=200ms for typical requests (<=512 tokens)
- Stability: <1% error rate under target concurrency
- Cost: estimated per-query cost within 15% of target

Open items (to confirm)
- Sample data delivery method and format (S3 or secure upload)
- Any specific compliance/regulatory requirements beyond SOC2
- Procurement timeline and PO process (cc'd procurement OK to loop)

Next steps
- I'll upload the success criteria & demo slides (attached) and share a SOC2 link.
- Can we target the week of Aug 16 for kickoff? If that works I will send a calendar invite and a short mutual action plan.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to tighten the scope.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0192 | dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

Attachments: POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx, Demo_Slides.pdf

From: Tom Chen <tom.chen@enterprisefin.com>

Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan - EnterpriseFin

Thanks Dylan — really helpful recap and the proposed cadence looks reasonable. A few quick clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Data residency: for the POC we can provide anonymized sample payloads, but for any live advisor traffic we need the instance to be in our VPC in us-west-2. Can you confirm Redwood can support that for the sandbox?
2) Sample size: you mentioned 50 curated prompts for functional checks — can you share the grading rubric so my lead will know how to score?
3) SLAs: for the POC we'll need a short-term SLO for latency and uptime — even 99% availability for the test window is fine, but we want to document expectations to avoid surprises.

We can probably do week of Aug 16. Procurement (procurement@enterprisefin.com) is looped for any contract/PO questions. Also please add our security contact if you need to transfer SOC2 evidence.

On the attachment, I don't see the rubric in the spreadsheet — can you resend with scoring columns?

Tom
Tom Chen
Head of Product | EnterpriseFin

On Mon, Aug 2, 2027 at 6:03 PM Tom Chen <tom.chen@enterprisefin.com> wrote:
> Thanks Dylan — really helpful recap and the proposed cadence looks reasonable. A few quick clarifications before we lock dates:
>
> 1) Data residency...

Hi Tom — great questions, short answers below and I've attached an updated success criteria spreadsheet with a scoring rubric and columns for reviewer notes.

1) Data residency: yes — we can spin up a sandbox in your VPC (us-west-2) for the POC. For the POC we'll use your VPC with customer-managed keys; Redwood will provide the image and runtime but no customer data leaves the VPC unless you opt-in.
2) Grading rubric: attached in the 'Scoring' tab — 0/1/2 per prompt with guidance; summary columns auto-calc pass rate
3) SLAs: for the POC we typically commit an internal test SLO (95th-pct <=200ms) and 99% availability for the test window. If you need contractual SLAs we can loop legal but that typically moves to Dedicated contracts.

I also added our SOC2 link above for the security team: https://redwood-inference.docs/soc2_report_v2.pdf

If Aug 16 works I'll send a kickoff calendar invite for Monday Aug 16 at 10am PT and a short MAP with owners / deliverables.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
